title: Why Playwright, and setting it up
summary: Install Playwright Test, understand what `npm init playwright@latest` creates, and how the pieces fit: test runner, browsers, config, reports.
why: As a manual tester you already know what to check. Playwright Test is the runner that executes those checks in real Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, in parallel, with auto-waiting, traces and reports built in — no extra libraries to wire together.
body:
Playwright Test (@playwright/test) bundles the runner, assertions (expect), fixtures and reporters. Browsers are downloaded separately with `npx playwright install` so their versions match the library exactly.

A new project has: playwright.config.ts (where tests live, base URL, browsers = projects, retries, reporters), tests/ (your *.spec.ts files) and, after a run, playwright-report/ and test-results/ (traces, screenshots).

In this hub you never install anything: the runner container is the official mcr.microsoft.com/playwright image for the pinned version, and the app under test runs next to it.
objectives: Know the three commands: init, install, test
Know that browser versions are pinned to the Playwright version
pitfalls: Upgrading @playwright/test without re-running npx playwright install.
Committing playwright-report/ and test-results/ — they are build output.

example.code:
# new project (choose TypeScript, tests folder, GitHub Actions workflow)
npm init playwright@latest

# or add to an existing project
npm install -D @playwright/test@latest
npx playwright install --with-deps   # browsers + OS dependencies

npx playwright test                  # run all tests headless
npx playwright test --ui             # UI mode
npx playwright show-report           # open the HTML report
